data.goal: A version bump merged to main is tagged, published to npm and announced as a GitHub Release by npm-publish.yml, with the CHANGELOG section in the notes

detail: R-a-release-whose-verify-failed-is-not-ret-d31f: A release whose verify failed is not retried by a later fix commit, and the workflow header does not say how to recover

data.title: A release whose verify failed is not retried by a later fix commit, and the workflow header does not say how to recover
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: A bump commit that goes red in verify (a missing CHANGELOG section, a real defect) is fixed by a commit that does not touch package.json, so the paths filter starts nothing and a re-run reuses the failed commit. The way out — pushing the tag by hand on the fixed commit — works but is not written in the header comment (review M1).
data.likelihood: likely on the first release that forgets the CHANGELOG section
data.fix: two lines in the header: after a red run, fix on main, then tag the fixed commit vX.Y.Z and push the tag

detail: R-an-empty-changelog-section-passes-the-re-7b94: An empty CHANGELOG section passes the release gate

data.title: An empty CHANGELOG section passes the release gate
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: A bare '## [X.Y.Z]' heading followed by the next heading makes the tool exit 0 with an empty body: the gate 'the CHANGELOG has a section for this version' is green and the Release carries the static text only (review M2, run by the reviewer).
data.likelihood: easy to do by accident; nothing wrong is published, the notes are just empty
data.fix: exit 1 when the trimmed body is empty, with a test

detail: R-one-concurrency-group-for-every-release-a626: One concurrency group for every release: a middle pending release can be dropped; a non-UTF-8 CHANGELOG exits 1 with a traceback

data.title: One concurrency group for every release: a middle pending release can be dropped; a non-UTF-8 CHANGELOG exits 1 with a traceback
data.label: INFERENCE
data.what: The group was release-<ref>, now it is the constant 'release': GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so with a run waiting on the npm approval and two later pushes the middle one is cancelled. Separately tools/changelog-section.py:55 lets UnicodeDecodeError escape (exit 1, traceback) where a usage error is exit 2 (review L1).
data.likelihood: rare: needs three releases queued; the gate is red either way for the decode error
data.fix: say so in the header comment; catch UnicodeDecodeError beside OSError

detail: R-a-prerelease-version-merged-to-main-is-t-bc54: A prerelease version merged to main is tagged and announced like a stable release

data.title: A prerelease version merged to main is tagged and announced like a stable release
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: A 1.2.3-rc.1 bump on main publishes under the dist-tag next, creates the tag and a GitHub Release without --prerelease, and the notes tell readers to run npx riskrails@latest, which does not install the rc (review L2).
data.likelihood: only when a prerelease version is merged to main
data.fix: pass --prerelease to gh release create for versions with a hyphen, or state the behaviour in the header

detail: R-gh-release-view-failing-for-any-reason-r-c6c0: gh release view failing for any reason reads as 'no release' in detect

data.title: gh release view failing for any reason reads as 'no release' in detect
data.label: INFERENCE
data.what: An auth, rate-limit or network error sets release=true where a Release exists; the run then goes red at 'not on the registry yet' or at gh release create, with nothing wrongly published (review L3: the safe direction).
data.fix: optional: tell 'release not found' from other errors

detail: R-tests-test-release-py-pins-the-release-w-2001: tests/test_release.py pins the release workflow by substring: gating and the detect logic are not exercised

data.title: tests/test_release.py pins the release workflow by substring: gating and the detect logic are not exercised
data.label: RISK
data.what: Not asserted: that publish has no if: (always() would defeat the gate), that notes.md receives the changelog and is the --notes-file, the release=false decisions and the awk parse of ls-remote (never run), an empty section, CRLF, --file on a directory (review L4).
data.likelihood: a later edit of the workflow could break gating with every test green
data.fix: assertNotRegex(publish, r'(?m)^\s+if:') and run the awk snippet on canned ls-remote output

detail: R-the-manual-tag-route-relies-on-github-no-e0c3: The manual tag route relies on GitHub not applying paths filters to tag pushes

data.title: The manual tag route relies on GitHub not applying paths filters to tag pushes
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: on.push now has tags, branches and paths together. GitHub's workflow-syntax page states 'Path filters are not evaluated for pushes of tags' (read 2026-11-12), so a pushed tag still starts the workflow; it was not exercised by a real tag push (review I1).
data.likelihood: would only change if GitHub changed the documented rule
data.fix: none; the first manual tag push after the merge confirms it

detail: R-an-annotated-tag-pushed-by-hand-github-s-54eb: An annotated tag pushed by hand: GITHUB_SHA versus the peeled commit in 'Create the tag' is unverified

data.title: An annotated tag pushed by hand: GITHUB_SHA versus the peeled commit in 'Create the tag' is unverified
data.label: UNKNOWN
data.what: The step compares the tag's peeled commit with GITHUB_SHA after npm publish has uploaded. For a lightweight tag (what this repository has used so far) they are the same commit; for an annotated tag it was not confirmed that GITHUB_SHA is the commit and not the tag object — a mismatch would fail the run after the upload (review I2). One real annotated-tag run answers it.
data.likelihood: only for annotated tags; every release tag so far is lightweight
data.fix: compare against git rev-parse HEAD of the checkout, which is always the commit
